A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same benchmark and training project, renamed ORLoopBench in v3. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial extensions.

before.justification: v1 reports original LP repair and newsvendor evaluations, training ablations, prompting comparisons, and failure analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds MILP repair, EOQ decisions, feedback experiments, architecture and decoding checks, and external-benchmark evaluations.

M1.justification: The core SFT/GRPO, LoRA, PRM, composite reward, and training curriculum remain. v3 adds cost-feedback quantity revision and a generate-then-repair pipeline that uses reference-objective diagnosis for incorrect formulations, extending the inference procedure beyond infeasibility repair (Appendix G.1).

E1.justification: v1's evaluated LP repair and newsvendor coverage expands to MILP repair across ten domains and eight error types, 300 EOQ instances, and decisions with repeated cost feedback. v3 also evaluates generation-plus-repair pipelines on NL4Opt, IndustryOR, MAMO Complex, OptMATH, and OptiBench, previously discussed principally as related work.

E2.justification: The original 26-model LP comparison remains, while v3 Table 33 adds Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.4 on LP repair. v3 also reports an OptiMUS-style whole-model regeneration comparison, which was not evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: The stated LP protocol changes from multiple episodes with diagnostic actions excluded from the budget to one 50-action episode counting every emitted action (v1 B.6/D.2; v3 C.6/E.2). Difficulty calibration switches from SFT/IIS-size targets to API-performance groupings. Added protocols include temperature sweeps, five-round cost feedback, and conditional second-stage repair. These reported changes do not establish that retained LP results were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds LP-to-MILP transfer checks, feasibility-versus-semantic-correctness analysis of regenerated code, architecture transfer, and decoding-temperature sensitivity (F.6–F.8). It supplies the per-error-type matrix that v1 offered only upon request. Existing RAG, reward-weight, curriculum-stage, and failure analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: v3 newly reports five repeated runs for MILP evaluation (Section 5.3 and Table 3). Both versions retain fixed-seed statements, training-reward standard deviations, and PRM correlation significance statistics. No confidence intervals or comparable uncertainty estimates accompany the new MILP summary.

E6.justification: The 26-row LP and 24-row newsvendor result tables are numerically unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results, including 78.8% zero-shot and 87.1% MILP-trained RR@5 versus Claude Sonnet 4.6's 71.0%. It adds regeneration, EOQ, transfer, and external-benchmark outcomes. Existing token figures also change: o4-mini tokens per success change from 7,985 in v1 Table 32 to 5,976 in v3 Table 34; this is a reporting revision, not an established performance gain.

T1.justification: The formal success-counting definition changes: v3 Algorithm 2 measures recovery within one episode, and its action-budget definition includes diagnostic queries previously excluded from RR@k. The underlying DA, reward, PRM-labeling, and newsvendor mathematics remain. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v3 makes MILP transfer and semantic drift in regenerated formulations central contributions in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. The headline LP advantage narrows from 95.3% versus 86.2% to 95.3% versus 92.4% after adding stronger comparators. The abstract's emphasis shifts away from curriculum training's supposedly unique negative OOD drift toward broader solver-guided repair reliability.

C2.justification: The new Discussion qualifies IIS as a potentially nonunique infeasibility certificate rather than a complete causal explanation, identifies unsupported formulation classes, and describes feedback-based inventory correction as an upper-bound diagnostic. v3 also explains semantic drift, qualifies deployment-cost claims, and corrects the PRM trade-off interpretation relative to SFT versus curriculum. Some overclaims about uniquely improving OOD bias remain.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the release-upon-publication statement with a concrete benchmark repository link and describes JSON organization, including the 4,462/450/450 record groups. It adds MILP domain and seed-separation information plus EOQ and external-pipeline instructions. The detailed core training, hardware, software, and inference configurations remain substantially unchanged; repository availability is reported by the PDF, not independently verified.

R1.justification: Section 6 and new Appendix A substantially revise positioning by discussing closely related OptiChat and OptiRepair systems, historical ANALYZE, and formulation approaches including SIRL, Autoformulation, OptiTree, and MIND. v3 qualifies v1's broad first/one-shot framing and distinguishes controlled constraint-level repair from prior interactive diagnosis and formulation systems.

P1.justification: Beyond the ORLoopBench renaming, the abstract, contributions, benchmark descriptions, training explanations, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Several main-text equations become prose explanations while their substance remains elsewhere. Related work is condensed in the main text and expanded in Appendix A, and a separate Discussion with limitations changes the narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figures 1–4 are redrawn, while Figure 5 retains its curves with a revised caption and placement. v3 adds substantial tables for per-type results, frontier comparisons, regeneration, architecture transfer, temperature sensitivity, and EOQ/external evaluations. Dataset and difficulty tables are restructured, and typography and float placement change throughout.

improvement.justification: v3 improves auditability through the formerly unavailable per-type results, stronger API comparisons, MILP transfer and semantic-drift checks, and clearer acknowledgment of close prior work and applicability limits. It also corrects the PRM trade-off description and several numerical summaries. However, unchanged LP scores are not reconciled with the revised protocol, Figure 5 and Table 37 contain unreconciled RR@1 values, and OOD-uniqueness claims remain contradicted by Table 40. These unresolved consistency issues limit the net quality improvement.
